#| label: init

library(tidyverse)

source("R/arc-models.R")

::: {.callout-note}
## Prerequisites
This notebook fits the contraction-expansion model (algo4) with logit-scale
noise to the Honig et al. experimental data using full Bayesian inference.
Each subject completed 4 sessions; here each subject–session combination is
treated as an independent unit. Model diagnostics and parameter recovery are
in [algo4 Bayesian diagnostics](diagnostics-algo4-bayes.qmd). The MLE
counterpart is in [algo4 MLE diagnostics](diagnostics-algo4-mle.qmd).
:::

## Model setup

```{r}
#| label: define-family-stanvars-priors
sdm_algo4 <- custom_family(
  "sdm_algo4",
  dpars = c("mu", "c", "kappa", "delta", "asigma"),
  links = c("tan_half", "identity", "log", "logit", "log"),
  type = "real",
  loop = FALSE,
  vars = c("vreal1", "vreal2")
)

stanvars <- sdm_base_stanvars() +
  stanvar(
    scode = read_file("stan/sdm_algo4_likelihood.stan"),
    block = "functions"
  )

prior <- set_prior("constant(0)", dpar = "mu", class = "Intercept") +
  set_prior("student_t(5, 2, 0.75)", dpar = "c", class = "Intercept") +
  set_prior("student_t(5, 1.75, 0.75)", dpar = "kappa", class = "Intercept") +
  set_prior("normal(-3.5, 2)", dpar = "delta", class = "Intercept") +
  set_prior("normal(-3.5, 2)", dpar = "asigma", class = "Intercept")


fit_algo4_bayes <- function(data, file) {
  brm(
    bf(resperr | vreal(half_arc, arc_next) ~ 1, c ~ 1, kappa ~ 1, delta ~ 1, asigma ~ 1),
    prior = prior,
    data = data, family = sdm_algo4, stanvars = stanvars,
    backend = "cmdstanr", cores = 4, init = 0, file = file,
    refresh = 0
  )
}
```

## Load data

Each subject completed 4 sessions. We treat each subject–session combination
as an independent unit by creating a `subject_session` identifier.

```{r}
#| label: load-data
honig <- read_csv("output/honig_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
dat <- honig |>
  mutate(subject_session = paste(subject, session, sep = "_")) |>
  select(subject, session, subject_session, trial, resperr, arc) |>
  arrange(subject, session, trial) |>
  mutate(half_arc = arc / 2, half_arc = if_else(half_arc > 0, half_arc, 1e-6)) |>
  group_by(subject_session) |>
  mutate(arc_next = lead(half_arc, default = -1)) |>
  ungroup()
```

## Single-subject fit (sanity check)

Select one subject–session to test the pipeline:

```{r}
#| label: fit-subject
unit_ids <- sort(unique(dat$subject_session))
s1 <- dat |> filter(subject_session == unit_ids[1])
fit_s1 <- fit_algo4_bayes(s1, file = paste0("output/fit-algo4-bayes-honig-", unit_ids[1]))
```

```{r}
#| label: fit-summary
summary(fit_s1)
```

## Plot posteriors on native scale

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| label: native-posterior-plot
algo4_posterior_draws <- function(fit, n_draws = NULL) {
  draws <- as_draws_df(fit) |> 
    select(starts_with("Intercept"), -Intercept)

  colnames(draws) <- gsub("Intercept_", "", colnames(draws))

  if (is.null(n_draws)) {
    idx <- seq_len(nrow(draws))
  } else {
    idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(draws)), size = n_draws)
  }

  draws |>
    mutate(c = exp(c), kappa = exp(kappa), delta = inv_logit(delta), asigma = exp(asigma)) |> 
    slice(idx)
}

algo4_posterior_draws(fit_s1) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "est")  |> 
  ggplot(aes(est)) +
  stat_halfeye(normalize = "groups") +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free")
```

## Posterior predictive check

```{r}
#| label: ppc-helpers
#| code-fold: true
algo4_sim_from_draws <- function(draws, data) {
  purrr::pmap(
    draws,
    \(c, kappa, delta, asigma) {
      run_arc_algorithm(
        arc_update_fun = algo4_logit_noise(delta = delta, sigma_e = asigma),
        c = c,
        kappa = kappa,
        init_arc = data$half_arc[1],
        n_trials = nrow(data)
      )
    }
  )
}

plot_algo4_ppc <- function(fit, data, n_draws = 15, draws = NULL) {
  if (is.null(draws)) draws <- algo4_posterior_draws(fit, n_draws = n_draws)
  sims <- algo4_sim_from_draws(draws, data)
  posterior_col <- grDevices::adjustcolor("red", alpha.f = 0.3)

  obs_median <- median(data$half_arc)
  pred_medians <- vapply(sims, \(s) median(s$a), numeric(1))
  pred_median_mid <- median(pred_medians)
  optima <- purrr::pmap_dbl(draws, \(c, kappa, ...) find_optimum_sdm(c, kappa)$alpha)
  optimum_mid <- median(optima)

  oldpar <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(oldpar), add = TRUE)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

  plot(density(data$half_arc), main = "Arc width distribution")
  for (sim in sims) {
    lines(density(sim$a), col = posterior_col)
  }
  lines(density(data$half_arc), lwd = 2)
  abline(v = optimum_mid, col = "blue", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
  abline(v = obs_median, col = "black", lwd = 2, lty = 3)
  abline(v = pred_median_mid, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 3)
  legend("topright",
    c("Data", "Posterior draws", "Optimal", "Obs median", "Pred median"),
    col = c("black", "red", "blue", "black", "red"),
    lty = c(1, 1, 2, 3, 3), lwd = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 2), bty = "n")

  plot(density(data$resperr), main = "Response error distribution")
  for (sim in sims) {
    lines(density(sim$y), col = posterior_col)
  }
  lines(density(data$resperr), lwd = 2)
  legend("topright", c("Data", "Posterior draws"), col = c("black", "red"), lty = 1, bty = "n")

  invisible(sims)
}

plot_algo4_ppc_trajectories <- function(fit, data, n_draws = 15) {
  draws <- algo4_posterior_draws(fit, n_draws = n_draws)
  sims <- algo4_sim_from_draws(draws, data)

  oldpar <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(oldpar), add = TRUE)
  par(mfrow = c(4, 4))

  plot(data$half_arc, type = "l", xlab = "Trial", ylab = "Arc half-width",
       main = "Data", ylim = c(0, pi), col = "blue")

  for (sim in sims) {
    plot(sim$a, type = "l", xlab = "Trial", ylab = "Arc half-width",
         main = "Posterior", ylim = c(0, pi))
  }

  invisible(sims)
}

summarize_algo4_posterior <- function(fit, unit_id) {
  algo4_posterior_draws(fit) |>
    pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "est") |>
    group_by(parameter) |>
    summarise(
      median = median(est),
      lower = quantile(est, 0.025),
      upper = quantile(est, 0.975),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(subject_session = unit_id, .before = 1)
}
```

We plot 15 posterior predictive distributions for response error and half arc-width.

```{r}
#| label: pp-arc-plot
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
plot_algo4_ppc(fit_s1, s1, n_draws = 15)
```

Here are different predicted arc trajectories with parameters drawn from the posterior vs the data (top left panel):

```{r}
#| label: pp-arc-traj-grid
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 10
plot_algo4_ppc_trajectories(fit_s1, s1, n_draws = 15)
```


## Unpooled fits to all subject–sessions individually

```{r}
#| label: fit-all-subjects
#| output: false
unit_ids <- sort(unique(dat$subject_session))

unit_data <- unit_ids |>
  set_names() |>
  map(\(uid) dat |> filter(subject_session == uid))

fits_all <- imap(
  unit_data,
  \(data, uid) fit_algo4_bayes(data, file = paste0("output/fit-algo4-bayes-honig-", uid))
)
```

Posterior 95 BCI for all subject–sessions and parameters

```{r}
#| label: posterior-summary
#| warning: false
posterior_smry <- imap_dfr(
  fits_all,
  \(fit, uid) summarize_algo4_posterior(fit, uid)
)

ggplot(posterior_smry, aes(subject_session, y = median)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper)) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 6))
```

Posterior predictives for all subject–sessions

```{r}
#| label: ppc-all-subjects
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-show: hold

iwalk(
  fits_all,
  \(fit, uid) plot_algo4_ppc(fit, unit_data[[uid]], n_draws = 15)
)
```

### Predicted vs observed arc summary statistics

```{r}
#| label: ppc-median-mad-arc
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 5
ppc_arc_summary <- imap_dfr(fits_all, \(fit, uid) {
  data <- unit_data[[uid]]
  draws <- algo4_posterior_draws(fit, n_draws = 100)
  sims <- algo4_sim_from_draws(draws, data)

  tibble(
    subject_session = uid,
    pred_median = map_dbl(sims, \(s) median(s$a)),
    pred_mad = map_dbl(sims, \(s) mad(s$a)),
    obs_median = median(data$half_arc),
    obs_mad = mad(data$half_arc)
  )
})

ppc_arc_pred_smry <- ppc_arc_summary |>
  group_by(subject_session, obs_median, obs_mad) |>
  summarise(
    pred_median_mid = median(pred_median),
    pred_median_lo = quantile(pred_median, 0.025),
    pred_median_hi = quantile(pred_median, 0.975),
    pred_mad_mid = median(pred_mad),
    pred_mad_lo = quantile(pred_mad, 0.025),
    pred_mad_hi = quantile(pred_mad, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p1 <- ggplot(ppc_arc_pred_smry, aes(x = obs_median, y = pred_median_mid)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = pred_median_lo, ymax = pred_median_hi)) +
  labs(x = "Observed median arc", y = "Predicted median arc",
       title = "Median arc width") +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(ppc_arc_pred_smry, aes(x = obs_mad, y = pred_mad_mid)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = pred_mad_lo, ymax = pred_mad_hi)) +
  labs(x = "Observed MAD arc", y = "Predicted MAD arc",
       title = "MAD of arc width") +
  theme_minimal()

p1 + p2
```


## Hierarchical fit

The likelihood handles subject–session boundaries via the `arc_next` column:
the last trial of each subject–session has `arc_next = -1`, so the Stan code
skips the arc-transition term for those rows. Each subject–session is treated
as an independent grouping unit.

```{r}
#| label: fit-hierarchical
hfit <- brm(
  bf(
    resperr | vreal(half_arc, arc_next) ~ 1,
    c ~ 1 + (1 | subject_session),
    kappa ~ 1 + (1 | subject_session),
    delta ~ 1 + (1 | subject_session),
    asigma ~ 1 + (1 | subject_session)
  ),
  prior = prior,
  data = dat, family = sdm_algo4, stanvars = stanvars,
  backend = "cmdstanr", cores = 4, init = 0, refresh = 0,
  file = "output/fit-algo4-bayes-honig-hierarchical"
)
summary(hfit)
```

### Extract subject-level posterior draws

We use `coef()` to obtain posterior draws of the subject–session-level
parameters (population intercept + random effect), then transform them to
the native scale.

```{r}
#| label: hier-subject-draws
#| code-fold: true
algo4_hier_subject_draws <- function(hfit, unit_id, n_draws = NULL) {
  coefs <- coef(hfit, summary = FALSE)
  idx <- if (is.null(n_draws)) TRUE else sample(nrow(coefs$subject_session[, , 1]), n_draws)

  tibble(
    c     = exp(coefs$subject_session[idx, unit_id, "c_Intercept"]),
    kappa = exp(coefs$subject_session[idx, unit_id, "kappa_Intercept"]),
    delta = inv_logit(coefs$subject_session[idx, unit_id, "delta_Intercept"]),
    asigma = exp(coefs$subject_session[idx, unit_id, "asigma_Intercept"])
  )
}
```

### Population-level posterior draws

```{r}
#| label: hier-population-draws
#| code-fold: true
algo4_hier_population_draws <- function(hfit, n_draws = NULL) {
  draws <- as_draws_df(hfit) |>
    select(b_c_Intercept, b_kappa_Intercept, b_delta_Intercept, b_asigma_Intercept)

  idx <- if (is.null(n_draws)) seq_len(nrow(draws)) else sample(nrow(draws), n_draws)

  tibble(
    c     = exp(draws$b_c_Intercept[idx]),
    kappa = exp(draws$b_kappa_Intercept[idx]),
    delta = inv_logit(draws$b_delta_Intercept[idx]),
    asigma = exp(draws$b_asigma_Intercept[idx])
  )
}
```

### Overall posterior predictive check

We simulate from the population-level parameters and overlay on the full
dataset distributions.

```{r}
#| label: hier-ppc-overall
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
hier_ppc_overall <- function(hfit, data, n_draws = 15) {
  draws <- algo4_hier_population_draws(hfit, n_draws = n_draws)
  sims <- algo4_sim_from_draws(draws, data)
  posterior_col <- grDevices::adjustcolor("red", alpha.f = 0.3)

  oldpar <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(oldpar), add = TRUE)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

  plot(density(data$half_arc), main = "Arc width distribution (overall)")
  for (sim in sims) lines(density(sim$a), col = posterior_col)
  lines(density(data$half_arc), lwd = 2)
  legend("topright", c("Data", "Posterior draws"), col = c("black", "red"), lty = 1, bty = "n")

  plot(density(data$resperr), main = "Response error distribution (overall)")
  for (sim in sims) lines(density(sim$y), col = posterior_col)
  lines(density(data$resperr), lwd = 2)
  legend("topright", c("Data", "Posterior draws"), col = c("black", "red"), lty = 1, bty = "n")
}

hier_ppc_overall(hfit, dat, n_draws = 15)
```

### Per-subject–session posterior predictive checks

For each subject–session we draw from their shrinkage-adjusted posteriors and
simulate arc-width and response-error trajectories.

```{r}
#| label: hier-ppc-per-subject
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-show: hold
iwalk(unit_data, \(data, uid) {
  draws <- algo4_hier_subject_draws(hfit, uid, n_draws = 15)
  sims <- algo4_sim_from_draws(draws, data)
  posterior_col <- grDevices::adjustcolor("red", alpha.f = 0.3)

  obs_median <- median(data$half_arc)
  pred_medians <- vapply(sims, \(s) median(s$a), numeric(1))
  pred_median_mid <- median(pred_medians)
  optima <- purrr::pmap_dbl(draws, \(c, kappa, ...) find_optimum_sdm(c, kappa)$alpha)
  optimum_mid <- median(optima)

  oldpar <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(oldpar), add = TRUE)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

  plot(density(data$half_arc),
       main = paste0("Arc width – ", uid))
  for (sim in sims) lines(density(sim$a), col = posterior_col)
  lines(density(data$half_arc), lwd = 2)
  abline(v = optimum_mid, col = "blue", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
  abline(v = obs_median, col = "black", lwd = 2, lty = 3)
  abline(v = pred_median_mid, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 3)
  legend("topright",
    c("Data", "Posterior draws", "Optimal", "Obs median", "Pred median"),
    col = c("black", "red", "blue", "black", "red"),
    lty = c(1, 1, 2, 3, 3), lwd = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 2), bty = "n")

  plot(density(data$resperr),
       main = paste0("Response error – ", uid))
  for (sim in sims) lines(density(sim$y), col = posterior_col)
  lines(density(data$resperr), lwd = 2)
  legend("topright", c("Data", "Posterior draws"), col = c("black", "red"), lty = 1, bty = "n")
})
```

### Per-subject–session posterior parameter summary (hierarchical)

```{r}
#| label: hier-posterior-summary
#| warning: false
hier_posterior_smry <- imap_dfr(unit_data, \(data, uid) {
  algo4_hier_subject_draws(hfit, uid) |>
    pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "est") |>
    group_by(parameter) |>
    summarise(
      median = median(est),
      lower = quantile(est, 0.025),
      upper = quantile(est, 0.975),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(subject_session = uid, .before = 1)
})

ggplot(hier_posterior_smry, aes(subject_session, y = median)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper)) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 6)) +
  ggtitle("Hierarchical model: subject-session posteriors (native scale)")
```
